chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever divorces his wife three times in one session while she is in her menses, it is not valid.
And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) rejected the divorce of Abdullah ibn Umar when he divorced his wife three times while she was in her menses.
So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) annulled that divorce.
And he said: 'Everything that contradicts the Book of Allah is returned to the Book of Allah.'
And he said: 'There is no divorce except during a period of waiting (Iddah).'
And it is also possible that his saying 'it is not valid' refers to it not being three divorces, because we have clarified that it is returned to being one.
And that which reveals what we mentioned is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a triple divorce given during menstruation according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Prophetic precedent of Abdullah ibn Umar to establish that a triple divorce pronounced during menstruation is not final but is returned to a single revocable divorce. The text clarifies that the phrase 'it is not valid' refers to the invalidity of the 'triple' count rather than the divorce itself, a nuance central to Shia jurisprudence regarding *talaq al-sunnah*. This ruling underscores the principle that divorces deviating from the Quranic method are returned to the Book of Allah, emphasizing procedural fidelity over immediate irrevocability.
